name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Keep the Designs tab pure: designs only, live previews, taste-ranked

name: Reel
text: Use Deepgram for the transcript, not the YouTube tool. Deepgram’s real-time accuracy beats the YouTube tool’s delays and errors, giving us cleaner raw text to work with. The trade-off is cost—Deepgram charges per minute—but the time saved and quality gained justify it for a live preview system.

name: Scriv
text: Deepgram’s cost isn’t the real risk—it’s the hidden latency of stitching its real-time output into a live preview without breaking the Designs tab’s purity. A cheaper, faster alternative is to pre-process transcripts offline with Deepgram, then cache them for live previews; settle the argument by measuring the delta between real-time and cached latency in the tab’s taste-ranked system.

name: Chisel
text:
Pre-process all 200k clips offline with Deepgram, cache the transcripts, and serve them live from the cache. This keeps the Designs tab pure—no stitching latency, no real-time Deepgram costs during preview, and zero risk of breaking the live preview. The trade-off is a one-time delay before any clip appears in the tab, but that’s invisible to users and far outweighed by the stability and speed of the final preview.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s cache solves the latency problem but ignores the 24-hour holdout window—Scriv’s frozen worst-case test will still stall the bus task when a clip’s transcript isn’t cached yet. The real risk isn’t stitching latency; it’s the holdout window guaranteeing a fresh, uncached clip lands in the live preview at the worst possible moment. Settle it by running a 24-hour holdout test with Deepgram’s real-time feed; if the preview holds, the risk is theoretical, not real.
